oneSentence: A label for the most capable and general-purpose AI models available at a given time, especially those seen as pushing technical limits and raising new governance questions.
plainExplanation:
People use this label for AI models that sit near the leading edge of what current systems can do. They are usually very large machine learning systems trained on vast datasets, and they can often handle many different tasks such as writing, coding, summarising, analysing images, or translating text. The boundary is not fixed. What counts as “frontier” changes as technology moves on.

What goes in is usually a prompt, image, audio clip, or other input. Inside the system, the model uses patterns learned from training data to predict a useful output, such as the next word, a label, a translation, or generated content. What comes out can look impressive, but it is still generated from statistical pattern matching rather than guaranteed fact.

The term is often confused with foundation model. A foundation model is a broad base model that can be adapted to many uses. A frontier model is a relative label: it points to the most advanced models available at a certain moment. Many frontier models are also foundation models, but not every foundation model is frontier.

The term is also often confused with artificial general intelligence, or AGI. Frontier models may perform strongly across many tasks, but that does not mean they have human-like general intelligence, consciousness, or reliable judgement. The word “frontier” says more about current capability and potential impact than about the system having a mind or broad understanding like a person.

everydayAnalogy.title: The newest all-purpose translation booth at an international conference
everydayAnalogy.story: At a large international conference, organisers test a new translation booth that can handle many languages, accents, and speech styles better than the older booths. Delegates speak into microphones, and the booth produces draft translations quickly for many sessions. Because it is the newest and strongest booth in the building, staff call it the one at the front edge of their equipment. But they still keep human interpreters checking difficult phrases, names, and sensitive statements.

mapping.analogyElement: The newest and strongest booth in the building
mapping.aiElement: A model considered among the most capable available at that time
Prompts or other inputs such as text, audio, or images
Human oversight because strong performance does not guarantee accuracy or suitability

everydayAnalogy.limitation: A translation booth is a single visible machine built for one clear purpose. Frontier models are not one kind of device, and they may generate text, images, code, or predictions across many tasks. Also, the analogy may suggest that “frontier” is an official technical threshold, when in practice the boundary is debated and shifts over time.

visual.title: Foundation model, frontier model, and AGI are not the same label
visual.learningObjective: After viewing, the reader should be able to explain that “frontier” is a moving label for leading capability, not a fixed technical category and not the same as AGI.
visual.description: A three-column comparison. Read left to right: a broad reusable model, a current leading-edge model, and a hypothetical human-level general system. Arrows show overlap between the first two, and a clear gap between frontier models and AGI claims.

steps.label: Foundation model
steps.explanation: A broad model that can be adapted to many tasks. It is defined by reuse across applications, not by being the strongest available.
steps.visualInstruction: Draw a left column box labelled 'Foundation model'. Inside, place small icons for text, image, code, and speech. Add a note: 'general-purpose base model'.

steps.label: Frontier model
steps.explanation: A model described as near the current limit of capability or scale. This is a relative status that can change as newer systems appear.
steps.visualInstruction: Draw a centre column box labelled 'Frontier model'. Use a highlighted outline. Add a timeline marker above it reading 'current leading edge'. Include the same task icons plus a note: 'moves over time'.

steps.label: Overlap
steps.explanation: Many frontier models are also foundation models, because the most advanced systems are often broad and reusable. But not every foundation model is frontier.
steps.visualInstruction: Add a double-headed arrow between the first and second columns. Beneath it, write 'often overlaps, not identical'.

steps.label: Not the same as AGI
steps.explanation: Strong performance across many tasks does not prove human-like general intelligence, consciousness, or dependable judgement in all settings.

workedExample.scenario: A regional business association wants help drafting short summaries of 12 public market reports in English, Arabic, and French.
workedExample.input: Prompt: 'Summarise each report in 100 words, list the top three trade trends, and translate the summary into Arabic and French. Flag any uncertainty.'
process: An organisation tests two models on the same public reports and prompt.
The more capable model handles all 12 reports, keeps the requested format, and produces usable drafts in all three languages.
Reviewers find that it still makes two unsupported claims and mistranslates one product name.
They classify it as a frontier model for their evaluation because it performs near the top of currently available systems, but they still require human review before use.
workedExample.result: The team gets faster draft summaries and translations, but not publication-ready material. The label 'frontier' helps describe current capability, not trustworthiness or full autonomy.

unWorkplaceExample.scenario: A UN office considers a highly capable model to produce first-draft translations of non-confidential field updates into a working language for internal review.
unWorkplaceExample.relevance: The term matters because leadership may hear that a system is 'frontier' and assume it is automatically suitable for operational use. In practice, the office still needs procurement checks, human review, quality testing for relevant languages, and compliance with organisational rules.
unWorkplaceExample.caution: Do not put confidential, personal, protection-sensitive, security-sensitive, or operationally sensitive field information into an unapproved public AI service, even if the service is described as frontier.

whyItMatters: For policy and leadership, this term often appears in risk, procurement, competition, and governance discussions. It can influence how people judge opportunity and danger. If you treat it as a precise scientific category, you may overestimate what a system can reliably do. If you ignore it, you may miss why some models attract special attention: they can be more capable, more widely deployable, and potentially more consequential than earlier systems. The key decision point is not whether a model is called frontier, but what evidence exists about its performance, limits, safety controls, access model, and appropriate uses.
whereYouMayHearIt: media coverage of new model releases

commonMisconceptions.misconception: A frontier model is simply any model with a very large number of parameters.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Size often matters, but the label is not based on one number. People use it for systems seen as near the leading edge of capability, scale, or impact at a given time. A smaller model could outperform a larger one on some tasks, and a large model may not be leading once better systems appear.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: If a model is called frontier, its answers are probably correct.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The label points to capability, not guaranteed accuracy. A frontier model may produce fluent summaries, code, or translations while still making factual errors, missing context, or giving unsuitable outputs. Stronger performance reduces some failures but does not remove the need for testing and human oversight.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Frontier model means the same thing as AGI.
commonMisconceptions.correction: No settled definition makes those terms identical. Frontier models are current leading systems; AGI usually refers to a hypothetical system with much broader, more human-like general capability. People disagree on AGI definitions, so using 'frontier' does not prove that such a threshold has been reached.

simpleVsTechnical.simple: A frontier model is one of the most advanced AI models available right now. It can often do many tasks well, but it is still a tool with limits and should not be treated as automatically reliable or human-like.
simpleVsTechnical.technical: In technical and policy use, 'frontier model' is a relative and time-dependent label for models near the current state of the art in capability, scale, or generality, often with potential for broad deployment and significant downstream effects. In practice, these are commonly large deep learning models trained on extensive datasets with substantial compute, and many are multimodal, meaning they can process more than one data type such as text and images. Inputs may include prompts, images, audio, or structured data; the model transforms these inputs into probability-based outputs such as generated text, classifications, translations, or action recommendations. The term does not name a single architecture, benchmark threshold, parameter count, or legal category. It is also not equivalent to 'foundation model', although there is frequent overlap, and it is not evidence of artificial general intelligence.

keyTakeaway: “Frontier model” means near the current leading edge of AI capability, not a fixed class, not a guarantee of truth, and not the same as AGI.

quickCheck.question: Which statement best captures what 'frontier model' usually means?
options: A model near the current leading edge of capability, often broad in use, but still requiring evidence and oversight
Any model that is open-source and available for anyone to download
A model that has reached human-like general intelligence across all domains
Any automated system used in government or large organisations
quickCheck.explanation: The term is usually used for models seen as among the most capable available at a given time. It is relative, not permanent. It does not mean the model is open-source, fully reliable, or equivalent to AGI.
